sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are that, on 13- 01-2020 at about 2.15 p.m., petitioner was riding his scooter, bearing No.KA-02-HZ-0708 slowly, carefully, cautiously observing all traffic rules and regulations proceeding on the left side of Magadi main road from KHB Colony towards Sumanahalli,
when he reached near Anant Bajaj Showroom, Kamakshipalya, at that time rider of Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle, bearing No.KA-02- JX-9405 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
without observing any traffic rules came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's scooter.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Boss Speciality Clinic and Diagnostic Centre, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 inpatient.

entities.text: Boss Speciality Clinic and Diagnostic Centre, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was working as Computer Hardware Service Engineer in Techsoft, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and whereby lost his earning capacity.
Therefore, petitioner prayed for compensation.
3. Respondent No.1 remained absent and therefore, he was placed exparte.

3(a) Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle, bearing No.KA-02-JX-9405 and its validity as on the date of accident, denied the other petition averments generally and it contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act, the rider of motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving licence to rode the same, the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of petitioner himself and also he was contributed to the cause of accident, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary and proper parties, the rider of scooter, bearing No.KA-02-HZ-0708 without wearing helmet and without having valid and effective driving licence rode the same on the date of accident.
Without prejudice it contended that motorcycle, bearing No.KA-02-JX-9405 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Further, it sought for permission to contest 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on 13-01-2020 at about 2.15 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Pulsar Motorcycle, bearing registration Sri Ramesh Babu R vs Smt. Except negligence, the incident, injuries, involvement of vehicles and issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.

The charge sheet/final report filed by the Kamakshipalya Traffic Police shows the negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle, bearing No. KA-02-JX-9405.

The accident was not due to the mechanical defect in the sense, then that could have been by the negligence only.

The wound certificate reveals one grievous and two simple injuries such as 1) swelling, tenderness, crepitus and deformity of left leg, 2) laceration present over palmar aspect of distal third of ring finger of right hand measuring 1.5 cm. x 1 cm. x 0.5 cm. margins are irregular and 3) abrasion over back of distal third of middle finger of right hand measuring 2 cm. Now whose negligence was there to the incident to be analyzed.
No 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 eyewitness is examined herein.
As already noted the final report shows the negligence was on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
Nothing is here in elicitation by respondent No.2 in cross examination of petitioner in supportive of it's version regarding the negligence.
Hence, without here being contrary evidence, here is no impediment to believe the police records.
So that, the police records are considered.

10. Regarding objections by respondent No.2 as to non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is concerned as the petition reached its finality and the petitioner approached the Tribunal, respondent No.2 had already taken all the contentions of respondent No.1 the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act, and discussion on the same now does not arise.
11. Regarding objection of respondent No-2 of non joinder of necessary party is concerned as final report came to be filed against the offending motorcycle the parties already arrayed are suffice.

12. Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that the petitioner met with motor vehicle accident on 13-01- 2020 at about 2.15 p.m., and sustained grievous and simple injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of 8 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 rider of motorcycle, bearing No.KA-02-JX-9405 .
Hence, this issue is answered affirmatively.

In proof of the 9 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 disablement he examined PW3 - Orthopaedic Surgeon from Sai Sri Ramesh Babu R vs Smt. Nagamma on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138447254/
4 Ortho and Dental Center, who assessed the disability of petitioner, opined that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability to the lower limb at 46% and to the whole body at 15%.

His evidences clear that he is not the treated doctor, it is stated that one more surgery is required to petitioner for removal of implants, which means that disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
In fact, as per the gazette notification issued by Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after the treatment is completed.

sentences.text:
As far as this case is concerned, if the disability would be assessed after the future surgery, perhaps,
there would have been reduction in the percentage of disability.
Therefore, it would say that the assessment of disability is premature and may be excessive.

Under the facts and circumstances of case, considering the elicitation in cross examination of doctor, having regard to the nature of injuries and the fracture came to be united, the disability to the whole body is taken to be considered at 10% as disablement as the disability assessed is an opinion of the doctor and no certificate of disability is produced from the competent authority.
10 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 Avocation
It is averred that the petitioner was working as Computer Hardware Service Engineer in Techsoft, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In substantiation of the same he produced salary certificate cum job left letter as per Ex.P14.
But, he has not examined the author of this document.
Hence it is not established that the petitioner was working as Computer Hardware Service Engineer.
Hence in the present case, avocation of petitioner is need to be considered notionally as he had notional income only.
Age As per Ex.P15 - driving licence, Ex.P16 - aadhar card and Ex.P17 - PAN card
, date of birth of petitioner was 30-12-1972 and so that, age of petitioner was 47 years at the time of incident.

Hence,
those are considered.
Income
As discussed on the head of avocation, the petitioner's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2020 came to be fixed at Rs.14,500/.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.14,500/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the petitioner, per month.
Considering the avocation and income notionally now loss of future income due to disability needs to be calculated.
According to the determined age of petitioner multiplier is 13.
So, 10% of monthly notional income comes to Rs.1,450/- x 12 months x multiplier 13 = Rs.2,26,200/- it is considered as compensation under the head of loss of future income due to the disablement.
Laid up period and Pain and sufferings
Petitioner was treated as inpatient from 13-01- 2020 to 18-01-2020.
He underwent operation.
He suffered fracture.
So that, he suffered pains and sufferings and also lost his earnings at the time of his treatment as well as his nourishment at least for the period of 3 months.
It is therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation considering his pains and sufferings and for his laid up period.

Hence, it is opined that 3 months' notional income of Rs.43,500/- + Rs.50,000/- for pains and sufferings = Rs.93,500/- will be just and proper in Sri Ramesh Babu R vs Smt. Nagamma on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138447254/

sentences.text: Medical Bills:
It is averred that petitioner incurred Rs.1,75,000/- for the treatment.
To prove the same, he produced 5 advance receipts, 21 prescriptions and 16 medical bills as per Ex.P11 to Ex.P13.
All those bills have been 12 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 examined with care and caution and found correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence, a sum of Rs.1,07,755/- is awarded towards medical expenses.
Amenities and happiness:
It is established that the petitioner sustained grievous injury.
The assessment of disability by the doctor and its consideration as discussed above are to be considered herein.
With such permanent disablement and surgical scars he will have to lead his future life.
From such injury he suffered pains, difficulties, which deprived him of leading his happy life and from enjoying amenities.
It is therefore, the petitioner is entitle for compensation for loss of his such amenities and happiness.
So, It is deemed proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

Food, Nourishment, Attendant charges and Conveyance:
Under the facts and circumstances of the case having considered the nature of the injuries and permanent disablement, though here is no document particularly, it could be presumed that the petitioner might have spent considerable amount for his nutritional food, nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance.
It is therefore, it is opined that for such food, nourishment, attendant charges and for conveyance is concerned awarding of Rs.30,000/- as 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 compensation is just and proper.
Hence, it is considered so.
Future medical expenses :
The evidence of the doctor reveals that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost approximately around Rs.60,000/-.
Herein being no estimation by the doctor, the expenditure that would costs in the government undertaking hospital for such surgery is considered and Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
14. Accordingly, details of compensations are as under:

Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs. 5,27,455-00 15.
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,27,455/-, which can be rounded off to Rs.5,27,500/-.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided 14 (SCCH-16) MVC 471/2020 under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization except future medical expenses.
So, the petitioner is entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.

Liability:
16. Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the rider of the offended motorcycle.
On vicarious liability respondent No.1 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.2 being the insurer of respondent No.1 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.2 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioner is only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
17.
In view of the findings, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,27,500/- (Rupees five lakhs, twenty seven thousand and five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
